content:
lila_peopleops: quick follow-up from today's all-hands Q&A thread. dropping the practical answers here so managers have something to copy into 1:1s and packets.
kelly_mgr: thanks! a couple managers asked for a one-liner to use when announcing promos and a short checklist for packets.
zach_eng: also saw a question about retro pay timelines and what happens if payroll cutoff is missed.
marco_total_rewards: I'll handle the comp/bonus bits. TL;DR up top: promos can be effective while someone is on leave, retro pay is to the effective date but depends on payroll cutoff, and equity vesting doesn't change automatically. Details below.

lila_peopleops: Retro pay & payroll timing
- we pay retro to the promotion effective date, not the approval date.
- payroll cutoff: if the promo packet is fully approved before payroll's cutoff for the next pay run, retro shows in that next run. if approvals miss that cutoff, retro is applied in the following pay run (usual lag 1 pay period).
- tip: include the desired effective date in the packet and flag "retro requested" to speed triage.

marco_total_rewards: Bonus & payout eligibility
- bonus eligibility uses the role/band that applies on the payout calculation date. if the promo effective date is earlier than that calculation date, the new band applies; otherwise the prior band does.
- proration: bonuses are prorated by days in band during the performance window. reach out to total-rewards for exceptions.

marco_total_rewards: Equity & RSUs
- existing grants keep their original vest schedules. promotions don't accelerate existing grants. any new grants tied to the promo follow the normal grant approval flow and will be documented separately.

lila_peopleops: Manager sign-off if manager leaves mid-process
- primary: skip-level manager signs.
- fallback: director or people-ops will sign to avoid blocking payroll. include a short decision note in the packet explaining who signed and why.

lila_peopleops: IC -> Manager transitions and holdbacks
- we usually set expectations in the packet about ramp; in some cases calibration asks for a short holdback (90 days) to make sure managerial skills are demonstrated. comp is adjusted at promotion; bonus/comp targets follow company policy and are pro-rated accordingly.

kelly_mgr: what about new hire compression? we had 1 case where a hire offer was higher than a teammate's comp.
marco_total_rewards: compression guidance
- we do not reduce current employees to fit a new offer. managers can request "compression review" via the comp queue. urgent cases can be flagged for off-cycle relief but those are evaluated case-by-case.

sophia_ceo: parental leave Q: does time on leave block promotions?
marco_total_rewards: promotions can be effective during leave. managers should include documented examples of prior work or cross-evidence. calibration may request extra context if the evidence window overlaps leave.

lila_peopleops: small manager checklist (paste into email/packet):
```
- Employee name, proposed title & band
- Effective date (YYYY-MM-DD) & "retro requested" flag if applicable
- Clear rationale + 2-3 concrete examples of impact
- Proposed comp (base + target bonus) and justification
- Signer name (skip-level if needed)
- Attach supporting docs (PR links, metrics, customer feedback)
```

lila_peopleops: short announcement script (one-line + optional follow-up):
"Congrats <name>! You're being promoted to <new title> effective <date>. This reflects your impact on <project/metric>. HR will send paperwork and payroll will reflect comp changes on the next pay run. Happy to answer questions"

zach_eng: that script is great 60a can we get a version for people on leave?
lila_peopleops: alternate for leave: "Congrats <name>. We're promoting you to <new title> effective <date>. We'll complete paperwork while you're on leave and confirm comp timing. Reach out if you'd like to discuss details when you're back."

people-ops-bot: Note: promo packet template v3 uploaded: https://drive.google.com/example-promo-template (auto message)

lila_peopleops: next steps: i'll publish a one-pager in #managers with these bullets and the template link by EOD tomorrow. also scheduling two 20-min office hours for packet walk-throughs (calendar invite soon). any objections?
sophia_ceo: none from me, thanks for the quick turnaround. :tada:
kelly_mgr: appreciate it. i'll forward this to my skip-levels.
marco_total_rewards: ping us in this thread if you hit a weird edge case; we'll triage.
